quote: Pretty good. But I think you guys did pretty did a pretty good job of tricking me into, clicking one too many times.
stewart_read: The customer is questioning the legitimacy of how his info was captured, essentially a soft version of the how-did-you-get-my-number concern. The rep never explicitly re-anchors the legitimacy of the form/lead source with honest specificity; he moves straight into disqualifying the interest instead of addressing the trust question.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged that re-litigating the lead source would waste time on a customer who was already exiting; letting it go was efficient. Rejected because the customer's underlying complaint (trickery) was never actually resolved, only the surface interaction was ended politely.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to use protocols.how_did_you_get_my_number honest-specificity framing even when the complaint is implicit, not just when directly asked — it can defuse the trust issue before deciding whether to pursue the call further.

quote: All I wanted to do I'm an engineer, so I love reading about, you know, alternate sources of energy and stuff like that.
stewart_read: This is a genuine, self-disclosed interest in solar technology from a technically literate customer — exactly the kind of curiosity that could be redirected toward 'let's get you real numbers for your home' rather than treated as noise ahead of a complaint.
coaching_implication: Flag for the rep: when a customer says they wanted to learn about the technology, that is an opening to redirect toward curiosity_over_features ('the design our specialist builds is specific to your home — that's the kind of detail you'd actually want to see'), not a signal to disengage.

quote: Mhmm. And so you're gonna pay a 150, $200 a month, which is, you know, what I pay in electricity now, which it it so it doesn't test the common sense test.
stewart_read: This is a textbook objection_inversion trigger: the customer states his current bill (150-200/month) as the reason solar doesn't make sense, when that same bill is the standard justification for switching. The rep never flips this — no acknowledgment of the number, no reframing that the same money is already being spent to the utility.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged the customer's mind was firmly closed and any flip attempt would read as pushy after the 'tricking me' comment. This is plausible, but the rep never even tested the flip once before conceding, so the reactive read (missed opportunity) is better supported than a deliberate strategic hold.
coaching_implication: This is also the clearest bill-anchor moment in the call — replay it with the rep and show how the $150-200 figure was volunteered and dropped without any acknowledge-and-flip attempt.

quote: And so, again, it was five years, so I thought I was clicking on getting the latest on technology about solar panels, that I could read about.
stewart_read: The customer restates, a second time, that his research is five years stale and that he wanted current information — practically inviting the rep to offer an updated look. The rep does not pick this up before moving to remove him from the list fifteen seconds later.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to hear repetition as emphasis: when a customer says the same thing twice in one call, it is the strongest signal in the transcript of what would actually re-engage them.

quote: Totally. Well, here, I can just take you off my list here, Charters.
stewart_read: The rep ends the call in under two minutes without asking a single verify-section item (bill, roof age/type confirmation, homeowner status) and without attempting any of the three natural openings the customer provided. This reads as a persistence gap (multi_angle_resilience) rather than a protocol-triggered exit — no protocol trigger phrase like a direct 'I'm not interested' or spouse/time objection was actually present.
alternative_hypothesis: Ending quickly could be read as respecting a clearly disinterested engineer's time and avoiding a pushy reputation hit. This has some merit given the customer's opening complaint about being tricked, but the customer's own repeated curiosity language undercuts a clean 'fully disinterested' read.
coaching_implication: Coach on multi_angle_resilience: target is 3+ angles per objection before conceding; this call shows zero angles attempted against three distinct openings.

quote: a slate roof. And so you you can't put you can't put solar panels on a slate roof.
stewart_read: The customer asserts a hard technical constraint (slate roof incompatible with solar) that the rep never confirms, questions, or routes for verification. This is exactly the kind of self-reported disqualifier that should be tested rather than accepted at face value, similar in spirit to the credit-qualifier stated-vs-verified concern in qualifiers.credit_qualifier.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may already know slate roofs are a standard hard constraint at Ion and considered it settled; no transcript evidence supports or refutes this technical claim, so it cannot be confirmed as correct rep judgment or a missed verification.
coaching_implication: Confirm with Kenny whether slate-roof claims should be taken at face value or routed to a specialist for confirmation before conceding the appointment.
